**30‑Day DBMS Mastery Plan** *(Designed for a beginner‑to‑intermediate learner who can study ~1–2 h per day)* --- ## How the Plan Is Structured | Week | Focus | What You’ll Do | |------|-------|----------------| | 1️⃣ | Foundations & Relational Model | Core concepts, ER modelling, basic SQL | | 2️⃣ | Advanced SQL & Normalisation | Complex queries, DML/DDL, normal forms | | 3️⃣ | Physical Design & Transactions | Indexes, storage, ACID, concurrency control | | 4️⃣ | Revision & Mini‑Project | Consolidate, practice exams, build a small DB app | Each day lists **Topic**, **Mini‑task**, and **Practice Q’s** (1‑3 short problems). Every **Saturday** is a *light‑review* day; every **Sunday** is a *full‑revision* day. **Week 4** ends with a 3‑day “Final‑Week” sprint that mimics an exam‑style test and a mini‑project showcase. --- ## Week 1 – Foundations (Days 1‑7) | Day | Topic & Sub‑topics | Mini‑task | Practice Q’s | |-----|--------------------|-----------|--------------| | 1 | **What is a DBMS?** – purpose, components, client‑server vs. embedded | Write a 150‑word summary; list 3 real‑world DBMS examples | 1. Define “data independence”. | | 2 | **Data models** – hierarchical, network, relational, NoSQL overview | Draw a simple hierarchy vs. relational diagram | 1. Which model best fits a file‑system? | | 3 | **Relational model basics** – tables, tuples, attributes, primary key | Create a paper table for a library (books, members, loans) | 1. Identify candidate keys in the library table. | | 4 | **Entity‑Relationship (ER) modelling** – entities, relationships, cardinalities | Sketch an ER diagram for the library system | 2. Convert the ER diagram to a relational schema. | | 5 | **SQL‑101 – SELECT** – projection, selection, WHERE, ORDER BY | Run SELECT queries on a sample SQLite DB (provided link) | 3. Write a query to list overdue loans. | | 6 | **SQL‑101 – FILTERING** – DISTINCT, LIKE, IN, BETWEEN, NULL handling | Modify previous queries to use each filter | 2. Find members who have never borrowed a book. | | 7 | **Saturday Light Review** – reread notes, redo Day 1‑6 queries | **No new material** – just a 30‑min quiz covering Days 1‑6 | 5 mixed‑question quiz (multiple‑choice + short SQL). | --- ## Week 2 – Advanced SQL & Normalisation (Days 8‑14) | Day | Topic & Sub‑topics | Mini‑task | Practice Q’s | |-----|--------------------|-----------|--------------| | 8 | **JOINs** – INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, SELF | Write one query for each join type using the library DB | 3. List books with their borrower names (including unborrowed). | | 9 | **Aggregation** – GROUP BY, HAVING, COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN/MAX | Build a report of total books borrowed per member | 2. Find members who borrowed > 5 books last month. | | 10 | **Subqueries & Set Operations** – EXISTS, IN, UNION, INTERSECT | Create a query using a correlated subquery | 2. Show members who have borrowed *all* books in a given genre. | | 11 | **Views, Stored Procedures, Triggers (intro)** | Create a view “OverdueLoans” and a trigger to log deletions | 1. Write the trigger code (pseudo‑SQL). | | 12 | **Normalisation – 1NF & 2NF** – functional dependencies, partial dependency | Normalise a denormalised “StudentCourse” table to 2NF | 2. Identify partial dependencies in the original table. | | 13 | **Normalisation – 3NF & BCNF** – transitive dependency, lossless join | Convert the 2NF design to 3NF, then to BCNF | 3. Explain why a given relation violates BCNF. | | 14 | **Sunday Full Revision** – redo all SQL queries, re‑draw ER/relational schemas, flash‑card review of normal forms | **Timed 45‑min mock test** (20 Q’s) | Review answers; note any weak spots. | --- ## Week 3 – Physical Design, Transactions & Performance (Days 15‑21) | Day | Topic & Sub‑topics | Mini‑task | Practice Q’s | |-----|--------------------|-----------|--------------| | 15 | **Storage & File Organisation** – heap, sorted, hash files | Sketch how a heap file stores rows | 1. Compare search cost for heap vs. sorted file. | | 16 | **Indexes** – B‑tree, clustered vs. non‑clustered, composite indexes | Build a B‑tree index on “ISBN” in SQLite (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN) | 2. When does an index hurt performance? | | 17 | **Query Optimisation** – cost‑based, EXPLAIN, join order | Run EXPLAIN on two different join orders; note differences | 3. Choose the cheaper plan for a given query. | | 18 | **Transactions & ACID** – atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability | Simulate a money‑transfer transaction in SQL (BEGIN…COMMIT) | 2. What happens on a power failure after BEGIN? | | 19 | **Concurrency Control** – locks (shared/exclusive), deadlocks, two‑phase locking | Identify a deadlock scenario in the library DB; propose a resolution | 1. Draw a lock‑compatibility matrix. | | 20 | **Recovery Techniques** – write‑ahead logging, checkpointing, rollback | Write pseudo‑code for a simple log‑based recovery | 2. Explain the role of a checkpoint. | | 21 | **Saturday Light Review** – index creation, transaction scripts, lock concepts | Quick 20‑question flash‑card set | No new coding; just recall. | --- ## Week 4 – Consolidation, Mini‑Project & Final Sprint (Days 22‑30) | Day | Activity | |-----|----------| | **22** | **Mini‑Project Kick‑off** – define a small DB (e.g., “Movie Rental”). Write requirements, ER diagram, and list of tables. | | **23** | **Schema Design** – normalise to 3NF, create SQL DDL scripts. | | **24** | **Data Population** – write INSERT statements (≈ 30 rows) and load into SQLite/PostgreSQL. | | **25** | **Feature Development** – implement 3 queries: (a) most‑rented movies, (b) overdue rentals, (c) revenue per month. | | **26** | **Advanced Feature** – add a trigger to prevent renting out‑of‑stock movies; test it. | | **27** | **Performance Tuning** – add indexes, run EXPLAIN, compare runtimes before/after. | | **28** | **Sunday Full Revision** – review all weeks, redo key practice questions, update flash‑cards. | | **29** | **Mock Exam** – 60‑minute timed test covering:
• Theory (30 %)
• SQL writing (40 %)
• Design/normalisation (30 %). | | **30** | **Project Showcase & Reflection** – run the mini‑project, record a short demo (or write a 300‑word report). List three topics you still need to revisit and plan next‑step study. | --- ### How to Use This Plan 1. **Stick to the daily time box** (≈ 1 h study + 15 min practice). 2. **Mark completed items** on a checklist; note any questions that linger. 3. **Every Saturday** keep the workload light – it prevents burnout. 4. **Sunday revisions** are the only “catch‑up” days; treat them as mini‑exams. 5. **Week 4** is deliberately project‑driven; building something consolidates every concept. --- **Need more detail?** - I can expand any day with step‑by‑step SQL code snippets. - I can provide a ready‑to‑run SQLite database file for the practice queries. - I can generate a full 60‑question mock exam with answers. Just let me know which part you’d like to dive deeper into!
